newsitem.title: UK: European bourses bask in Wall St's warmth.
newsitem.headline: European bourses bask in Wall St's warmth.

text.p: European bourses traded strongly higher on Monday, boosted by a solid advance on Wall Street which took lingering worries about interest rates in its stride.
All three of Europe's major bourses -- London, Paris and Frankfurt -- closed well up, with British shares ending within a few points of record levels.
Concerns about U.S. interest rates sparked by the release of jobs data last Friday appeared to calm as markets priced in a likely 0.25 percentage point rise in rates later this month.
"The Street is becoming convinced the Fed's going to tighten rates and an increase of 25 basis points is built in," Larry Wachtel of Prudential Securities in New York said.
The dollar stuck around 1.49 marks and 109 yen throughout much of the European session as a string of U.S. economic data due this week kept a lid on activity.
Despite U.S. rate speculation, foreign exchange traders were unwilling to take positions until at least after the Federal Reserve releases its Beige Book economic statement on Wednesday.
The Beige Book should provide the markets with clues on wage inflation in the United States, which could be an important factor when the Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24.
"People are looking for a 25 basis point (U.S. rate) rise but if the inflation figures are low, it still could tip the balance," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Bank in London.
Any rate rise should help the dollar but is likely to weigh on stock markets because investors might be tempted to switch out of equities and into bonds.
Britain's blue chip FTSE 100 index pushed back above 3,900 and to within sight of its record high, as inflation worries on both sides of the Atlantic eased.

Benign UK inflation data helped cheer sentiment in London and the FTSE 100 finished the session 17.8 points higher at 3,910.8. It was 7.9 points off its closing high and 11.3 points from its intraday peak, both set on August 28.

"I think the FTSE is set for record highs this week but at present the market is not blowing the socks off traders...this week's U.S. data is giving investors new cause to worry," said Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe Ltd.

Bullishness over shipping group P&O's container merger with Nedlloyd and BTR's disposals programme helped lead the FTSE 100 higher with P&O ending the session 42-1/2p higher at 559-1/2p. BTR closed with a gain of 4-1/2p to 266-1/2p.
Germany's IBIS DAX index ended at 2,549.71 after the 30-share DAX ended bourse trade up 1.26 percent at 2,548.73.
Shares in car-maker Volkswagen closed seven marks higher at 555.25 marks after a weekend German press report that it planned to boost its meagre return on sales.
French stocks closed 0.78 percent higher, helped by firmer bond prices and good corporate results.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 15.55 points at 2,020.30, while the CAC-40 September futures contract closed six points higher at 2,022.50. Volume was 3.89 billion francs.
Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel rallied 3.18 percent to close at 8.10 francs after reporting an operating breakeven for the first half of 1996.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4942 marks and 109.17 yen, compared with 1.4913 marks and 109.32 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was up 17.8 points at 3,910.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 31.73 points, or 1.26 percent, at 2,548.73. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index was up 6.97 at 2,549.71.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 15.55 at 2,020.30.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed softer at $383.55, down $2.10. Silver finished easier at $5.09, off six cents.
